clue.text: Justification given by one interrupting singer

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one item sits inside the other

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An excuse offered by a singer who keeps butting in.
explanation.walkthrough: BASS takes I after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the grounds or underlying reason offered to support an action or claim.

clue.text: Composer, upper-class, turned up in person in street

indicators.note: in places those reversed letters inside the word for person

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person
U is the classic label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Maurice Ravel, the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: A posh composer appears in person on a city street.
explanation.walkthrough: The upper-class marker joins the composer before both are turned, so it ends up first; a bod is British slang for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulevard is a broad city street, often lined with trees.

clue.text: Insolence in smooth and villainous tone, huge error in speech

indicators.note: and joins the second piece on after the first
in places the word for insolence inside the word for smooth

parts.note: soft means smooth to the touch
lip is cheek or insolence

indicators.note: villainous means crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky, slick villain's menacing tone, followed by a big blunder in speech.
explanation.walkthrough: S(LIP)OFT supplies the first seven letters; the rest come from the jumbled pair of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the tongue is an accidental mistake made while talking, saying a wrong word.

clue.text: Solid part in rehearsed manoeuvre

parts.note: set means solidified, as jelly sets
a piece is a part

explanation.surface: A firm role within a practised routine.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a set piece is a planned, practised move such as a corner or free kick.

clue.text: Listless learner, I gather, suffering with cold

indicators.note: something suffering is damaged or out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
taken as written
C stands for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: A sluggish pupil, apparently laid low with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gather' reads as an aside, but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lethargic lacks energy and enthusiasm, which is exactly what listless describes.

clue.text: Weapon, look, no good

indicators.note: no good tells us to remove the letter that abbreviates good

parts.note: a glance is a quick look

explanation.surface: Inspecting a weapon and finding it useless.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the usual abbreviation for good; take it from the front of GLANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a knight on horseback.

clue.text: Inferior article about one on road with informer

indicators.note: about means surrounding what follows

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places one piece directly above the next
with adds the next piece alongside

parts.note: Roman numeral one
RD is the abbreviation for road
a rat is someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: A poor newspaper piece about someone on the road with a snitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article, which wraps the other three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of poor quality, well below the best, so inferior.

clue.text: Awning usable at regular intervals yearly

indicators.note: at regular intervals means taking every other letter, skipping the ones between

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A sunshade that can be put up now and then each year.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annual happens once every year, the adjective yearly in another word.

clue.text: Dog, familiar in type, leapt finally with energy into stream

indicators.note: with attaches the next letter alongside
in places the word for familiar inside the word for type

parts.note: a genre is a type or category
as in an old friend, someone familiar

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word before it is kept

parts.note: finally picks the last letter

indicators.note: into means put inside the word for stream

parts.note: a river is a stream of water
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dog of a well-known breed jumps energetically into a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar' here is not a witch's cat but the old of 'old friend'; two separate containers build the two words of the breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden retriever is a popular breed of gun dog with a golden coat.

clue.text: Exclamation over platinum in vault

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a cry is an exclamation
Pt is the chemical symbol for platinum

explanation.surface: Someone shouts on finding precious metal in a strongroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' suggests a bank's strongroom; it is the underground chamber of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground chamber or vault beneath a church, used for burials.

clue.text: Accidentally popular number, latest from vocalist in association with partner

indicators.note: with means the next piece is simply added on at the end
the words before it are placed inside the group that follows

parts.note: a union is an association of people
what is in is fashionable or popular
a number

indicators.note: the latest from a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of vocalist
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A hit record that came about by chance, with a singer working alongside a collaborator.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like music-chart news, but 'popular number' is two separate pieces, not a hit song; the first three pieces combine to mean purpose before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unintentionally means doing it without meaning to, which is what happens by accident.

clue.text: Revolutionary book that is full of verse arousing intense feeling

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for book is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: something full of another thing holds it inside

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: A radical book packed with poetry that stirs the emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a description of the book's politics, but it turns the book round; i.e. is Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive subject or word is one that stirs up strong emotions in people.

clue.text: Face religious group, ignoring singular form of language

indicators.note: to ignore the singular is to leave out the letter that abbreviates singular

parts.note: a dial is a face, as on a clock
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: Confronting a religious group that disregards one particular way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular, dropped from SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional or social variety of a language, one particular form of it.

clue.text: Cross after anarchic act in capital leads to disappointment

indicators.note: after places the cross at the end, behind the other pieces

parts.note: an antic is a wild, absurd piece of behaviour
Lima is the capital of Peru; in places it after the act
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A wild stunt in a city sets up a let-down, cross being the angry mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry; it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax is a disappointing ending after a build-up of expectation, a letdown.

clue.text: Unlucky guys taken in by silly old lie

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside what follows
silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
guys are men

explanation.surface: Some unfortunate fellows are fooled by a foolish old falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-omened means accompanied by bad omens, so doomed or unlucky.

clue.text: Completion of filming western followed by strike

indicators.note: followed by puts the second piece straight after the first

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west or western
to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: A cowboy film finishes shooting, then the crew walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action in the film world, but it means a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: Film crews say 'that's a wrap' when shooting finishes, so a wrap is the end of filming.

clue.text: Favoured arbiter made a mistake under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the following pieces beneath the letter for pressure

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
a ref, referee, is an arbiter
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A referee who favours one side slips up under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favoured' looks like an accusation against the referee; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferred means liked better or chosen first, so favoured over others.

clue.text: Politician breaking hearts with start of spending squeeze

indicators.note: with adds the next letter at the end
breaking means bursting into the middle of something

parts.note: cores are hearts or centres
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: start of picks out only the first letter

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A politician breaks hearts by cutting public spending.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests austerity politics; 'hearts' are the centres of things and 'squeeze' is the definition, not a budget squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: To compress is to press or squeeze something into a smaller space.

clue.text: Proper time for performance by two

parts.note: due means fitting or proper, as in due care
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The right moment for a pair to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a piece of music played or sung by two performers together.

clue.text: Fly down by trunk keeping dry

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol, or dry

explanation.surface: An insect drifts down beside a tree trunk that stays dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry for teetotal is a crossword convention: someone dry drinks no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a large buzzing blowfly with a metallic blue body.

clue.text: Reason to accept large part of contract

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in

parts.note: a cause is a reason
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Grounds to agree to a big section of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a separate section or provision within a legal contract.

clue.text: Difficulty with bishop in part contained by head of government

indicators.note: in places the bishop inside the following word

parts.note: PM, the Prime Minister, heads the British government

indicators.note: contained by means held within the outer letters that follow

parts.note: a part in a play is a role
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Trouble arises when a bishop takes a role under the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, the bishop inside the part and both inside the head of government; PM is the Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem is a matter or situation that causes trouble, a difficulty to be overcome.

clue.text: Sauce essential to recipe stockpiled

indicators.note: essential to means found at the core of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A key sauce ingredient kept in bulk in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheese and oil.

clue.text: Get around parking strip

indicators.note: around means wrapped about the item that follows

parts.note: to derive is to get or obtain
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Driving around a car park looking for a space on a strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' sits at the end looking like a noun, a parking strip; it is the verb, to strip someone of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone is to take something away from them, to strip them of it.

clue.text: Nymph not interesting flier?

parts.note: dry means dull and uninteresting
a flier is an advertising leaflet, an ad

explanation.surface: A dull winged creature, perhaps, mistaken for a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'flier' is not something with wings but a printed leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph in Greek mythology, a spirit of the woods.

clue.text: Are young viewers prepared for film star?

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or worked up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether children are ready to see a celebrity's film.
explanation.walkthrough: Sigourney Weaver is the American actor of the Alien films, which many young viewers would not be ready for.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigourney Weaver is a famous Hollywood actor, best known as Ripley in Alien.

clue.text: Without fixed limits, start over

parts.note: to open is to start
over means finished

explanation.surface: No boundaries, so begin again from scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start over' reads as one phrase meaning restart; it splits into two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-ended has no set limit or predetermined conclusion, like an open-ended question or contract.

clue.text: Scrap with Romeo dividing cast

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the other word by sitting inside it

parts.note: to cast off, as skin, is to shed
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out with the actor playing Romeo splitting the theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' and 'Romeo' suggest a play; cast is the verb shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny scrap or fragment, as in not a shred of evidence.
